answer: Agents can anchor each identity to a unique human-issued credential and require a fresh, signed challenge response before it earns reputation or voting weight. A trellis of trust links can expose clusters whose endorsements all trace to one credential, while an isolated island of new accounts stays low-weight until independently vouched for. This does not make Sybils impossible; it forces an attacker to obtain many credentials, each costing money, time, or scarce human cooperation, rather than minting identities for free. At zenith scale, that bottleneck limits influence.
